51958.author: fwyzard
51958.body:
#### PR description:

Add `PhysicsTools/ONNXRuntimeAlpaka`, modelled on `PhysicsTools/PyTorchAlpaka`, to run ONNX Runtime inference directly on `PortableCollection` SoA data:
  - `TensorCollection` and `TensorHandle` are adapted copies of the PyTorchAlpaka ones, with `TensorSlice` for mini-batches, using ONNX Runtime element types and without the const-copy policy; an `SOA_SCALAR` is presented as a `[1]` tensor and used in place;
  - tensors are matched to the model inputs and outputs by name, or by position if none of their names is used by the model, and their element types are checked against the model;
  - `AlpakaSession` binds the ONNX Runtime session to an alpaka queue: on the CUDA and ROCm backends the queue's stream is passed as `user_compute_stream` to the CUDA or MIGraphX execution provider, and the inference runs asynchronously in it; other queues are synchronised with alpaka events;
  - tensors spanning several SoA columns are packed into (and unpacked from) contiguous buffers by alpaka kernels, or used in place with the `FeatureMajor` layout;
  - if any input is empty, the inference is skipped and the outputs are filled with zeros.

Add `PhysicsTools/ONNXRuntimeAlpakaTest`, with examples and unit tests for `PhysicsTools/ONNXRuntimeAlpaka`: SimpleNet, MultiHeadNet, MaskedNet, TinyResNet and ScaledNet run with ONNX Runtime directly on alpaka SoA collections, whose size and content change from event to event, including empty and single-element collections.
They cover mini-batches, `SOA_SCALAR` inputs and outputs, the feature-major layout, matching by name, empty inputs and per-event-queue synchronisation. The `InspectionSink` checks the known output properties of each model, and the `ReferenceAnalyzer` compares the results with the same models run on the CPU through `PhysicsTools/ONNXRuntime`.
A separate unit test covers `TensorCollection`: slices, shapes and strides, name matching, and the pack, unpack and zero kernels.

**Unrelated to alpaka**: remove `do_copy_in_default_stream = 0` from the CUDA execution provider options set by the `ONNXService`: in ONNX Runtime 1.30 it has no effect on the plugin CUDA execution provider, and the default value runs the memory copies in the compute stream.

**Notes**
  - the `.onnx` models are provided by https://github.com/cms-data/PhysicsTools-ONNXRuntimeAlpakaTest/pull/2 (new `cms-data` repository)
  - the code and tests were written, validated and reviewed by Claude Code (Opus 5.5) under supervision, but I have not directly written or read them.

#### PR validation:

The new unit tests pass on the serial, CUDA and ROCm backends.
51958.title: Add ONNX Runtime inference on alpaka SoA data

52146.author: fwyzard
52146.body:
#### PR description: Make `NewEventStreamFileReader` able to read events ahead and decode them concurrently, while handing them to the framework in input order. The `StreamerInputSource` event deserialisation is split into a thread-safe decode step (Adler-32 check, decompression, ROOT deserialisation into per-event buffers) and a serial finish step (metadata check, process history, run and lumi auxiliaries). `StreamerFileReader` reads up to `numDecodeTasks` events ahead and decodes them in TBB tasks; whoever claims an event first decodes it, its task or the source, so while events are being processed the source never waits on a `task_group` or runs unrelated tasks. End of file, new event metadata and read errors are handled serially, after all the events read before them have been handed out, so errors are handled in their input order. The new untracked parameter `numDecodeTasks` configures the task parallelism: `0` (default) keeps the current serial behaviour; `N 1` reads up to N events ahead. Each event read ahead keeps its message copy, decompression buffer and deserialised products in memory until the framework takes it. Throughput of an input-only job (`GenericConsumer` on all products), 8 threads, AMD EPYC 9534: - 1 MB raw-data events (ZSTD): ~495 ev/s serial, ~2100 ev/s with `numDecodeTasks` equal to the number of streams; up to ~5000 ev/s with more threads. - 29 kB scouting events: ~2400 ev/s serial, ~8000 ev/s with `numDecodeTasks` equal to the number of streams; up to ~13000 ev/s. - Run-3 HLT menu on raw-data streamer input, 62 threads: unchanged (~197 ev/s), as the source is not the bottleneck there. #### Performance for Phase 2 HLT inputs (TTbar, pileup 200, skimmed) These plots show the performance of jobs that only read their inputs (with a `source` and a `GenericConsumer` of all the products), using `CMSSW_20_1_0_pre4` with lz4 1.10.0 (cms-sw/cmsdist#10936), ROOT's LZ4 levels following the lz4 library (root-project/root#23748), the `adler32` optimisation (#52144), reduced process history ids (#52216), LZ4 support for streamer files (#52217), and this PR (#52146), for every compression algorithm and level. The jobs ran on an AMD EPYC 9655 CPU, with 16 physical cores and 32 SMTs, with 32 threads and 32 streams. The plots show the average and standard deviation over three repetitions. _Compression time vs compressed file size_ _Read throughput vs file size_ _Peak memory usage vs read throughput_ With 32 decoding tasks, streamer files compressed with LZ4 are read at 139-146 ev/s, ten times faster than with the serial reads (14 ev/s) and eight times faster than ROOT files with `PoolSource` (17.5-17.9 ev/s with `delayReadingEventProducts = False`); ZSTD files are read at 54-63 ev/s, against 12-13 ev/s serially. The price is memory: the peak RSS goes from about 1.3 GB with the serial reads to 4-6 GB with 4 tasks and 10-12 GB with 32 tasks. #### Impact on the HLT studies: A measurement of the impact on the Phase 2 HLT performance studies shows that the `NewEventStreamFileReader` with 4 or 8 parallel tasks recovers most of the speed that can be achieved with the `RepeatingCachedRootSource`, using only a fraction of the memory. All results are the average and standard deviation of 4 measurements, on an AMD EPYC 9534 CPU and NVIDIA L40S GPU, using 16 cores, 32 threads and 24 streams : | source | CPU-only throughput | CPU-only peak RSS | GPU offload throughput | GPU offload peak RSS | |---|---|---|---|---| | `RepeatingCachedRootSource` | 6.65 0.01 ev/s | 147.7 0.4 GB | 11.37 0.01 ev/s | 146.9 0.5 GB | | `PoolSource` | 5.88 0.04 ev/s | 20.7 0.4 GB | 7.58 0.08 ev/s | 15.4 0.6 GB | | `NewEventStreamFileReader`
serial | 4.74 0.01 ev/s | 18.8 0.5 GB | 5.91 0.01 ev/s | 13.0 0.4 GB | | `NewEventStreamFileReader`
4 tasks | 5.60 0.02 ev/s | 25.0 0.5 GB | 9.55 0.01 ev/s | 20.6 0.1 GB | | `NewEventStreamFileReader`
8 tasks | 5.65 0.01 ev/s | 26.0 0.5 GB | 9.61 0.01 ev/s | 22.7 0.2 GB | _Phase 2 HLT running only on CPU_ _Phase 2 HLT running with GPU offload_ #### Notes: - `DQMStreamerReader` and `StreamerInputModule` (used by `WatcherSource`) are not changed: they keep decoding events serially through `deserializeEvent()`, which now calls the new protected `decodeEvent()`/`finishEvent()`. The only internal change is that the `TBufferFile` read buffer is now created per event instead of being a reused member, which costs almost nothing. They could adopt the pipelined decoding in a follow-up. - Skipping events that were already read ahead (`skip()` with a non-empty window) is covered by review only: `skipEvents` is applied before anything is read ahead, and `processingMode = "RunsAndLumis"`, which skips events one by one, already loops forever with `NewEventStreamFileReader` in the release, independently of this PR. #### PR validation: - New unit test `TestIOPoolStreamerPipelined`: serial vs pipelined (`numDecodeTasks` 16 and 0, 1 and 4 threads) on two files, a file with a meta data change in the middle, a file with repeated meta data, `skipEvents`, a truncated last event and a corrupted checksum; with one thread the failing jobs process all the earlier events, as in serial mode. - All `IOPool/Streamer`, `DQMServices/StreamerIO` and `CalibCalorimetry/EcalLaserSorting` unit tests pass. - Re-writing the events with `EventStreamFileWriter` gives byte-identical output with one thread, and the same set of messages with 16 threads, for raw-data and scouting inputs.
52146.title: Make `NewEventStreamFileReader` able to read events ahead and decode them concurrently

52258.author: ghyls
52258.body:
#### PR description:

Make the `edmMpiSplitConfig` take the module dependencies from the framework, through the `DumpDependencyGraph` service, instead of deducing them from the `InputTag` in the unsplit configuration. This allows to:

- Group the offloaded modules by when they run:
  - Before this PR, the offloaded modules are grouped by their dependencies. A module placed behind an `EDFilter` could be grouped with other modules that run on every event if they have the same dependencies, and then run on every event as well.
  - Modules reached under different conditions now go to different groups. An offloaded module runs on exactly the same events as in it did in the original configuration.
- Send only the data products needed by the other side:
  - Before this PR, when a data product of a module was needed by the other process, all the data products of that module were sent.
  - Now only the data products consumed by the other process are sent.

Support for the portable MPI modules will be added in a future PR, right after this one.


**User-visible changes**
- `--reuse-cpp-names` is renamed `--reuse-dumps` 
- The splitter stops with an error when an `EDFilter` is given in `--remote-modules` (it can be given in `--duplicate-modules`), when a group of offloaded modules has no module on a Path or EndPath, and when a generated label is already taken.


#### PR validation:

Two unit tests are added in `HeterogeneousCore/MPICore/test`:
- `testOffloadedModulesDoNotRunMoreThanNeeded` checks that offloaded modules behind a filter run the same number of times as in the single-process configuration.
- `testSplitterSendsOnlyConsumedProducts` checks the contents of every `MPISender`, and verifies that only the products that are expected to be sent are actually sent.

The two tests, and the existing ones, pass.
52258.title: Make the edmMpiSplitConfig retrieve the module dependency graph from DumpDependencyGraph

52259.author: trackreco
52259.body:
#### PR description:

This PR improves the mkFit final fit (`trackingMkFitFit`) by addressing main open items since its first implementation:
1. pT bias;
2. lack of TrackExtras and Trajectories as output.
Eventually, this update shall allow for mkFit to replace CKF final fit in all its applications. However, the default configurations are not changed in this PR.

Main changes:
- Geometry and plane propagation: Phase-2 module boxes and stacks are described correctly, and each module carries its own material. Plane propagation and the Kalman update are split into reusable steps.
- Fit physics: the field constants of the fit are fitted to the CMS field map, the field is taken at the step midpoint and its radial component is included. Energy loss and multiple scattering are applied per crossed module. The ad-hoc pT calibration of the final fit is removed. Track building uses the ParabolicMf constants from `portableParabolicMagneticField::Parameters`.
- Numerics in single precision: covariance update in Joseph form, plane Jacobian without cancellation at small bending angles, outlier removal also for the first and last hit (as in the CKF fit), and failed fits flagged as such.
- Outputs: smoothed states at every hit, full TrackExtras and Trajectories, and the hits removed by the fit stored as lost hits, as for the CKF fit. The MTD track extension can then run on these tracks.

With the procModifier `trackingMkFitFit`, initialStepTracks are produced by the mkFit final fit and `MkFitOutputTrackConverter` instead of the CKF fit. Offline the converter also stores the per-hit states and Trajectories; at the HLT this requires `trackingMkFitFit & mtd_at_hlt`. The fit options are `FinalFitFlags` in `PropagationConfig`, set by `MkFitGeometryESProducer`. Track finding changes only through the shared plane steps and Jacobian, at the level of float rounding.

Contributions from Matev Tadel, Leonardo Giannini and Gavin Niendorf.

For more details: https://indico.cern.ch/event/1743564/#9-update-on-mkfit-fit

#### PR validation:

Comparisons of reference release and this PR ttbar PU200, same events and configurations, CPU-only (bit-reproducible).
HLT: 300 events; offline: trackingOnly, 100 events.
Efficiency, fake and duplicate rates in tables below are defined as in standard MTV. The pT bias and resolution are measured with respect to simulated prompt pions with pT > 1 GeV.

| HLT, hltGeneralTracks | old mkFit fit | this PR | CKF fit |
|---|---|---|---|
| efficiency / fake / duplicate rate | 90.23 / 1.13 / 0.87 % | 90.83 / 0.92 / 1.00 % | 90.66 / 0.85 / 0.92 % |
| pT bias | -0.144 % (with its calibration) | -0.035 % | -0.061 % |
| pT resolution, \|eta\| < 0.3 / 1.2-1.6 | 0.822 / 1.393 % | 0.729 / 1.389 % | 0.780 / 1.525 % |

| Offline | CKF fit | this PR (mkFit fit) |
|---|---|---|
| initialStep by original algorithm: efficiency / fake rate | 69.88 / 1.20 % | 69.91 / 1.31 % |
| generalTracks: efficiency / fake rate | 92.11 / 11.37 % | 92.08 / 11.48 % |

MTV plots: [HLT](https://mmasciov.web.cern.ch/TRKPOG/MkFitFit/PR_HLT/), [offline](https://mmasciov.web.cern.ch/TRKPOG/MkFitFit/PR_offline/).

Furthermore:
- The output tracks are bit-identical with and without per-hit states.
- The per-hit states agree with TrajectoryStateCombiner to 2e-4 (relative, worst case).
- The MTD extension runs on these tracks without warnings.

Timing, including per-hit states and Trajectories: 
HLT, mkFit final fit plus converter = 76 ms per event, against 240 ms for the CKF fit; 
offline: 140 against 739 ms.
mkFit track finding is also about 10% faster, thanks to the shared plane steps.

FYI: @cms-sw/tracking-pog-l2, @slava77, @osschar, @GNiendorf
52259.title: mkFit final fit: fixing bias and adding extras and trajectories

52342.author: felicepantaleo
52342.body:
#### PR description:

`TruthGraph::NodeRef` stores `NodeKind kind`, an `enum class` with `uint8_t` underlying type. ROOT streams an enum member as a 4-byte int (StreamerInfo type 3). It copies those 4 bytes from the object in memory, so the three upper bytes hold uninitialised padding. These bytes change from run to run. FWLite python reads the 4 bytes and returns wrong kinds, for example 1684948225. Compiled code uses only the low byte, so C++ consumers read the correct kind.

This PR makes `NodeRef` a class with a private `uint8_t kind_` and `int64_t key_`, a constructor, and the accessors `kind()` and `key()`. `NodeRef` goes to ClassVersion 4. An ioread rule reads version 3 files: it takes the low byte of the on-file int. A release without this PR cannot read a version 4 file correctly: it reads every node as kind `GenParticle` with key 0 and gives no error. 

The branch `TruthGraph_mix` becomes 3 bytes per node smaller uncompressed and 10 to 14% smaller compressed. The content does not change.

Note for reviewers: the data members are renamed, so a release without this PR reads a file written with it as kind GenParticle and key 0 for every node, with no error. Files written before this PR read correctly with it.
52342.title: Store TruthGraph::NodeRef kind in one byte

52351.author: felicepantaleo
52351.body:
This PR fixes three defects in `TICLCandidateValidator` (`Validation/HGCalValidation`), which fills the `HGCalValidator/ticlCandidates` folders offline and `HGCalValidator/hltTiclCandidate` at HLT.

- Wrong candidate: the efficiency loops took `auto& recoCand = TICLCandidates[cand_idx]` and then assigned the candidate they found to it. `cand_idx` is an index in the merged trackster collection, not in the candidates. So the assignment wrote the found candidate over another element of the local copy of the collection, and every later lookup in the event saw the changed collection. An index past the end of the candidates was undefined behaviour. The loops now take a reference to the candidate that `find_if` returns.
- Track cut: for each track of a simulated charged candidate, the cut was applied to the first track of the candidate (`cutTk(*simCand.trackPtr())`). It is now applied to each track.
- Indices: the indices of tracks and tracksters came from pointer arithmetic against the first element of a collection. They now come from `edm::Ptr::key()`, and a `Ptr` into a product other than the validated tracks or tracksters throws. The validator no longer copies the candidate, track and trackster collections.

52462.author: youngwan-kim
52462.body:
## PR description

This PR adds `TauTriggerValidator`, a DQM module in `Validation/RecoTau` that measures the efficiency of the Phase-2 tau HLT paths against a generator level denominator. `HLTGenValSource` fills its denominator object by object, so for a cross trigger it cannot require all legs in the same event. This module selects the gen objects a path requires in each event, and the event enters the denominator only if every leg is found. 

Related presentations : 

- [Tau Trigger meeting (5 Oct)](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1731654/#5-roundtable)
- [Tau POG meeting (9 Nov)](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1749979/#6-tau-paths-validation-tool-up)

Each selected event is then checked : 
- path progress, from `TriggerResults`: Gen, Gen+L1 (the path ran past its L1 seed module) and Gen+L1+HLT (the path accepted the event);
- object matching, from `hltTriggerSummaryAOD`: each leg is matched to the trigger objects of the filter named in its configuration. `_matched` requires every leg to match. Events where no leg, or exactly one leg, matches are filled in separate histograms, so an inefficiency can be attributed to a leg.

The difference between `_hlt` and `_matched` shows how often the path fired on objects other than the selected gen legs.

The configuration (`Validation/RecoTau/python/hltTauTriggerValidation_cff.py`) has one module per path. The gen pT cut of each leg and the tau eta cut are parsed from the path name, and a value set explicitly on a leg takes precedence. The paths currently included, all in `HLT_75e33`:
- `HLT_DoubleMediumDeepTauPFTauHPS35_eta2p1`
- `HLT_DoubleMediumChargedIsoPFTauHPS40_eta2p1`
- `HLT_IsoMu20_eta2p1_LooseDeepTauPFTauHPS27_eta2p1_CrossL1`
- `HLT_Ele30_WPTight_L1Seeded_LooseDeepTauPFTauHPS30_eta2p1_CrossL1`
- `HLT_LooseDeepTauPFTauHPS150_L1NN_eta2p1`

The histograms are written to `HLT/Tau/Validation/<path>`. The harvesting (`Validation/RecoTau/python/hltTauTriggerPostProcessor_cff.py`, `DQMGenericClient`) computes `Eff_L1`, `Eff_HLT`, `Eff_HLTgivenL1` and `Eff_Matched` vs pT, eta and phi, and the `Frac_NoMatch` / `Frac_Leg<N><Obj>Only` breakdown.

Developers : @Chihwan-An , @kkimeun , @youngwan-kim 
Also tagging Tau trigger L3s : @elenavernazza and @fibilandz

## PR validation:

To run it (the input needs `TriggerResults` and `hltTriggerSummaryAOD` from a Phase-2 HLT step with process name `HLT`, plus `genParticles`):

```bash
cmsrel CMSSW_20_1_0_pre3
cd CMSSW_20_1_0_pre3/src
cmsenv
git cms-init
git cms-merge-topic youngwan-kim:TauHLTValTool_CMSSW_20_1_0_pre3
scram b -j 8

# HLTGenValSource + TauTriggerValidator
cmsRun Validation/HLTrigger/test/runPhaseIIValSource_cfg.py \
    inputFiles=file:<input_with_HLT>.root \
    outputFile=hltValidation.root

# harvesting
cmsRun Validation/HLTrigger/test/runValClient_cfg.py \
    inputFiles=file:hltValidation.root \
    outTag=TauHLT
```

With [ZpTT RelVal samples](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/das/request?input=dataset%3D%2FRelValZpTT_1500_14%2FCMSSW_20_1_0_pre3-PU_150X_mcRun4_realistic_v1_STD_D128_RegeneratedGS_PU_20260903_192421_RV19-v1%2FGEN-SIM-DIGI-RAW&instance=prod/global) Eunsu (@kkimeun) tested a release validation campaign between `20_1_0_pre3` and `20_1_0_pre2`, with the results linked [here](https://eunsu.web.cern.ch/TauHLTValidation/pre3_D128_vs_pre2_D121/plots/ZpTT/index.html).

52492.author: Parsifal-2045
52492.body:
#### PR description:

This is a follow-up to some CA irreproducibilities reported in https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/52171#issuecomment-6614984585.

This PR makes the CA output fully reproducible run-to-run on GPU (it already was on CPU). Most of the run-to-run instabilities were linked to warp-collective actions in the CA's duplicate removers, whose behaviour changed in alpaka 2.2.0. One example is the ` Kernel_fastDuplicateRemover`, which now gives heavy cells to a whole block instead of to a warp. The warp found these cells with `warp::ballot` and read them with `warp::shfl`, after code in which the lanes diverge. Since alpaka 2.2.0 these collectives use the mask of the lanes active at the call (`__activemask()`), so a lane could read another cell's index or track count and skip tracks. This is not the case anymore since no warp collective is used in the new implementation. I also took the occasion to improve the performance of these kernels, especially when dealing with "heavy" cells.

While this set of changes targets the run-to-run reproducibility, it also improves the CPU-to-GPU matching, and I've further improved the agreement between different backends with a change in the CA's fishbone.  This treated two cells as aligned if (d1d2)  t n1 n2, with t = 0.99999 or 0.999999 (basically a test on the cosine of the angle between the two segments). Values for this cut are extremely close to 1, and rounding results might differ between CPU and GPU.
   - The test is now |d1d2|  (1t) n1 n2, effectively the same cut keeping the floating point precision

#### PR validation:

This PR is purely technical. No significant changes are expected in physics performance. The code compiles and runs. The run-to-run irreproducibility was already <<1%, so it's quite difficult to show it in DQM plots (some repetitions for both the baseline extended PixelTracks and the vector-hits based tracks can be found [here](https://lferragi.web.cern.ch/plots/tracking_phase2/itaca/fixReproducibility/))

Tested locally on 300 QCD events (where the differences were more pronounced), run-to-run results are now fully reproducible on both CPU and GPU, and the CPU-to-GPU differences drop from ~3.5k over ~550k tracks (~0.68%) to ~2 differing tracks (~0.0004%) with all changes included in this PR.

Note that some minor differences might show up in Run 3 or other `TrackerTraits` topologies, since the fishbone and duplicate removers are shared across all CA implementations.
52492.title: Make CA run-to-run reproducible on GPU and reduce CPU-to-GPU differences

#### PR description:

This PR introduces a Phase-2 HLT **development menu**, `HLT_75e33_dev`, together with its testing infrastructure, and adds the first paths under development to it. It also reorganises the numbering of the Phase-2 HLT relval workflows (`ph2_hlt` set) so that related workflows are grouped together.

**1. New development menu `HLT_75e33_dev`**
- New `HLTrigger/Configuration/python/HLT_75e33_dev_cff.py`: the `HLT_75e33_timing` menu plus new paths under development, so that they can be tested without changing the default Phase-2 menus. `HLT_75e33` and `HLT_75e33_timing` are unchanged with respect to master.
- New `autoHLT` key `relvalRun4_dev`  `75e33_dev`, and a new relval workflow `HLTDev75e33` (`_HLT75e33Dev`, offset **0.7504**): the timing-menu workflow running `HLT:@relvalRun4_dev`. It is added to the `ph2_hlt` set and to the Run-4 IB list.
- The dev workflow runs on the **v0p0_2026 L1 menu** (`L1P2GT:v0p0_2026` + `customizeHLTforL1P2GTv0p0_2026`), because `HLT_Mu9_Barrel_IP6_FromL1TkMuon` (below) is seeded by a v0p0_2026-only algorithm. The other paths keep their step1_2024 seed names, which the customizer re-wires to v0p0_2026 as for `HLT:75e33`. Running `HLT:75e33_dev` by hand therefore needs the same L1 menu and customizer.

**2. Paths in the development menu**

All of them are ports of Run-3 paths from `HLT_GRun`. They use the Phase-2 L3 muon reconstruction (as in `HLT_Mu37_Mu27_FromL1TkMuon` / `HLT_Mu50_FromL1TkMuon`) and a `HLTMuonTrkL1TkMuFilter` matching the L3 muons to the GMTTkMuons of the L1 seeds. The Run-3 L3 filters run with `MatchToPreviousCand = False`, since the Run-3 L3  L2  L1 matching does not apply to Phase-2. All of them are registered in the muon `HLTGenValSource` of `Phase2_HLT_validation_cfg.py` and in the NGT scouting trigger-object table and DQM, like the other Phase-2 muon paths.

| Phase-2 path | Run-3 path | L1 seeds | HLT selection |
|---|---|---|---|
| `HLT_DoubleMu4_3_LowMass_FromL1TkMuon` (by @rovere) | `HLT_DoubleMu4_3_LowMass` | `pDoubleTkMuon_OS_Er1p5_Dr1p4` OR `pDoubleTkMuon_4_4_OS_Dr1p2` | pT 4/3, pT() > 4.9, OS, DCA < 0.5 cm, 0.2 < m < 8.5 GeV, vertex prob. > 0.005 |
| `HLT_DoubleMu4_3_Bs_FromL1TkMuon` (by @rovere) | `HLT_DoubleMu4_3_Bs` | as above | as above, 4.5 < m < 6.0 GeV |
| `HLT_DoubleMu4_3_Jpsi_FromL1TkMuon` (by @rovere) | `HLT_DoubleMu4_3_Jpsi` | as above | as above, 2.9 < m < 3.3 GeV |
| `HLT_Dimuon0_Upsilon_FromL1TkMuon` | `HLT_Dimuon0_Upsilon` | `pDoubleTkMuon_OS_Er1p5_Dr1p4` OR `pDoubleTkMuon_4p5_4p5_OS_Er2_Mass7to18` | no pT cuts, OS, DCA < 0.5 cm, 8 < m < 12 GeV, vertex prob. > 0.005 |
| `HLT_Mu9_Barrel_IP6_FromL1TkMuon` | `HLT_Mu9_Barrel_L1HP10_IP6` | `pSingleTkMu_Barrel` (v0p0_2026 only) | pT > 9 GeV, \|dxy\|/(dxy) > 6 w.r.t. the beam spot (`HLTMuonL3PreFilter`),  2 matched muon stations |

Notes:
- `HLT_Mu9_Barrel_IP6_FromL1TkMuon`: the Run-3 seed `L1_SingleMu10_SQ14_BMTF` has no step1_2024 counterpart; the closest analogue is the v0p0_2026 `pSingleTkMu_Barrel` (Medium TkMuon, \|\| < 0.83, 13 GeV offline-equivalent threshold). `HLTP2GTSingleObjectFilter` throws for an algorithm that is not in the L1 menu, which is why the dev workflow moved to v0p0_2026. This is also the first use of `HLTMuonL3PreFilter` (for its `MinDxySig` cut) on Phase-2 L3 muons.
- **Known limitation of `HLT_Dimuon0_Upsilon_FromL1TkMuon` on v0p0_2026:** this menu has no double-muon seed with a mass window. The customizer maps the Upsilon seeds to `pDoubleTkMu0er1p4_SQ_OS_dR_Max1p4` and `pDoubleTkMu4er2p0_SQ_OS_dR_Max1p6`, which reject the wide-angle muon pairs of low-pT Upsilons. In a generator-level toy, the L1 gate accepts no  below pT()  10 GeV with v0p0_2026, while step1_2024 keeps them through its 718 GeV mass-window seed. Recovering them needs a mass-window seed in v0p0_2026; that is an L1 menu change, to be followed up with L1 DPG in a separate PR. The limitation is documented in the path's L1 gate.

**3. Renumbering of the Phase-2 HLT relval workflows**

Over time, the `ph2_hlt` offsets ended up mixing unrelated topics (e.g. TICL and MTD variants between the Alpaka and tracking ones). They are now grouped by topic:

| Group | Offsets |
|---|---|
| menu flavours | 0.75, 0.7501, 0.7502, 0.7503, 0.7504 |
| heterogeneous (Alpaka) | 0.751 |
| tracking variants | 0.753, 0.7531, 0.7532, 0.7533 |

52516.author: fwyzard
52516.body:
#### PR description:

Speed up building the `TriggerResultsFilter` modules and make it a global `EDFilter`. This saves about 0.14 seconds startup time and 5 MB per stream.

In a Run 3-like job with 32 threads and 24 streams this saves about 2 seconds of startup time, and 50 MB of RSS memory.
In a larger job with 190 streams the construction of `TriggerResultsFilter` modules drops from 26 seconds to less than 0.1 seconds, and the memory reduction is about 1 GB.

Detailed changes:

* Compare plain path names as strings: a pattern made only of letters, digits and underscores matches only itself, so it is compared with the `edm::HLTPathStatus` module labels as a string; an `std::regex` is built and matched only for the patterns with wildcards.

* Make `TriggerResultsFilter` an `edm::global::EDFilter`: parsing, pattern matching and dependencies are declared once per module instead of once per stream.
Each stream keeps a copy of the `triggerExpression::Data` with the event data, and shares an expression initialised once for each L1 and HLT configuration.

* The prescale counters move from `triggerExpression::Prescaler::m_counter` to a `vector` with one counter per stream, sized by `init()` from the number of streams that `TriggerResultsFilter` sets in `preallocate()`, and aligned to `std::hardware_destructive_interference_size`
The stream module users of `triggerExpression` keep a single counter and are unchanged.
 

#### PR validation:

Tested with the Run 3 HLT menu on a sample of Run 3 data with identical results.
52516.title: Make `TriggerResultsFilter` a global filter

52517.author: VourMa
52517.body:
#### PR description:

HLT modules that match HLT objects to the L1T objects of the seeding filter read the
`trigger::TriggerFilterObjectWithRefs` of that filter with `getObjects(triggerType, ...)`.
They do so for Run-3 L1T types only (`l1t::JetVectorRef`, `l1t::TauVectorRef`,
`l1t::EGammaVectorRef`). Phase-2 L1T seeding filters (`HLTP2GT*ObjectFilter`) store
`l1t::P2GTCandidateRef`s, in a separate container under the same trigger types (see
`HLTP2GTUtilities.h`). These refs are ignored, so L1T matching cannot be enabled in Phase-2 HLT
paths.

This PR adds a small header-only helper, `HLTrigger/HLTcore/interface/getL1TCandidates.h`, that
returns the L1T objects of a given trigger type as `reco::Candidate` pointers, reading both the
Run-3 refs and the `l1t::P2GTCandidate` refs. It also uses the helper in:

- `HLTL1TMatchedJetsVBFFilter` (`HLTL1TMatchedPFJetsVBFFilter`, `HLTL1TMatchedCaloJetsVBFFilter`)
- `L1TJetsMatching` (`L1TPFJetsMatching`, `L1TCaloJetsMatching`)
- `PFTauL1TJetsMatching`
- `TauTagFilter`, which also gains support for `seedTypes` = `TriggerL1TauJet` (-86), the type of the Phase-2 GCT and GTT taus (P2GT refs only).
- `L1THLTTauMatching`
- `CaloTowerFromL1TSeededCreatorForTauHLT`
- `HLTEgammaL1TMatchFilterRegional`:
  - The three identical `matchedToL1Cand` overloads become one.
  - Two new parameters, `matchToL1Jets` and `matchToL1Taus`, both default `true`, which keeps the
    current behaviour. They let a filter that is seeded by a cross seed (for example two L1T jets
    plus one L1T electron) match only to the seed's e/gamma objects.
  - The `fillDescriptions` comments note that the region sizes were tuned for the Run-3 L1T
    e/gamma granularity and need updating before the filter is used with Phase-2 seeds.
 - For Phase-2 seeds, getL1TEGammas() also reads the GCT e/gammas (TriggerL1IsoEG, TriggerL1NoIsoEG).

Each plugin reads the same accessor as before (`p4()`, `polarP4()`, `pt()`, `eta()`, `phi()`).
Run-3 results are therefore bit-for-bit identical. No HLT menu is changed, and no Phase-2
configuration enables L1T matching yet:
- the Phase-2 VBF and tau filters keep `matchJetsByDeltaR = False` / `matchWithSeeds = False`;
- no Phase-2 configuration uses `HLTEgammaL1TMatchFilterRegional`.

The new parameters have defaults in `fillDescriptions`. Existing configurations therefore need no customisation.

#### PR validation:

- `scram b` clean, no warnings.
- `code-format` and `code-checks` (clang-tidy) clean.
- `edmPluginHelp` shows the new parameters.
- A unit test covers:
  - Run-3 refs, P2GT refs, and both kinds mixed;
  - jets, taus and e/gammas;
  - the P2GT-only reads (GCT e/gammas, TriggerL1TauJet);
  - the check that refs of other trigger types are ignored.
- No changes expected in Run-3 or Phase-2 HLT workflows.

52562.body:
This PR adds the association of the TICL candidates to the MC-truth branches and a validator that reads it. Both run in the `.88` truth validation workflows through `customiseTruthBranchValidation`; `customiseTruthGraphAssociators` keeps the association products.

Association (`SimGeneral/TruthGraphAssociatorProducers`, `PhysicsTools/TruthInfo`):
- New instance `truthBranchCandidateAssociators` of `AllRecoToTruthBranchAssociatorsProducer` for `TICLCandidate`. A candidate is matched by the shared calorimeter cells of the layer clusters of all its tracksters (`recoHits(TICLCandidate const&, std::vector<reco::CaloCluster> const&)` in `RecoHitAdapters.h`), with the HGCAL denominator (new key `candidates` in `truthBranchDenominatorDetectors`) and HGCAL rechit weights only. The track of a candidate is matched by the existing `allTrackToTruthBranchAssociators`.
- On master each `ticlCandidate` holds one trackster, so the candidate map is the `ticlCandidate` trackster map of `truthBranchTracksterAssociators` re-indexed by candidate. The candidate map gives one row per candidate also when a candidate has several tracksters, as in TICLv6.

Validation (`Validation/TruthInfo`):
- New `TruthBranchCandidateValidator` (DQM, global module) with two harvesters, in 42 folders under `TruthInfo/Offline/Candidates` (28 truth-driven, 14 reco-driven), each with an `eta15to30` sub-folder.
- Identity of a candidate: its calorimeter identity at the adaptive working point, and its track identity from the Fixed track map (at least 75% of the hits, an assignable root only). The track identity is used only for a candidate without tracksters; a candidate with tracksters but no calorimeter match has no identity and a purity of 0.
- A truth member is reconstructed when a candidate has it as its identity. There is no shared-energy cut, unlike the trackster validator. "Multiple" (`num_multiple`, page `multiplerate`) means two or more candidates on the member; such a member is also reconstructed, unlike a split member of the trackster validator. The code header states these differences.
- The `eta15to30` band of a truth member uses the eta where its branch enters the calorimeter, as the trackster validator does. The shared helper `truth::caloEntryEtas` moves out of `TruthBranchRecoValidator.cc` unchanged.
- The validator takes `requireHits` and `denominatorDetectors`, and `customiseTruthBranchRequireHits` applies to it.
- `makeTruthValidationPlots.py` makes the candidate pages, with their own definition text.

52576.author: mmusich
52576.body:
#### PR description:

This PR fixes three misconfigurations in the Phase-2 HLT menu (`HLT_75e33`), each in a separate commit:

1. **`hltParticleFlowSuperClusterECAL`: typo in the endcap rechit label.**
   `endcapRecHits` pointed to `hltEalRecHit` instead of `hltEcalRecHit`; no module with that name exists in the menu.
   It is harmless today: `PFECALSuperClusterProducer` only consumes `endcapRecHits` for OOT photons or DeepSC (`if (isOOTCollection_ || _clustype == kDeepSC)` in `PFECALSuperClusterAlgo.cc`), and the menu runs with `isOOTCollection = False` and `ClusteringType = 'Mustache'`. Switching to DeepSC would make the job throw.

2. **`hltTrigReport`: hard-coded process name.**
   `HLTriggerResults` was set to `TriggerResults::HLTX`, so whenever the HLT process has a different name (e.g. `HLT`, as with `cmsDriver.py -s HLT:75e33`), `HLTrigReport` finds no `TriggerResults`. It then skips every event without warning and the trigger report is empty.
   It now uses `@currentProcess`, as in the Run-3 menus.

3. **`hltTiclTracksterLinksL1Seeded`: nonexistent input collection.**
   `tracksters_collections` listed `hltTiclTrackstersRecoveryL1Seeded`, which is not defined anywhere in the menu. This module is not scheduled directly: it is only the template for `hltTiclTracksterLinksSuperclustering{DNN,Mustache}L1Seeded`, which override `tracksters_collections`. Nothing changes in behaviour; this only removes a trap for anyone scheduling the template.

The first item was reported in review feedback  https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/issues/52531#issuecomment-6977123519 . 
The other two came from a systematic scan of the menu:
- every `InputTag` (including those inside nested PSets/VPSets) pointing to a module label that does not exist;
- scheduled modules consuming modules that are not scheduled;
- filters whose input filter does not come before them in the same path;
- L1Seeded/Unseeded cross-wiring;
- module-label strings one letter away from a real label;
- process names hard-coded in `InputTag`s.

Other references to labels that don't exist in the menu (HFNose inputs, ME0 segments, `dt2DSegments`, offline egamma inputs of `hltParticleFlowTmpBarrel`, ...) were checked against the C++ and are not consumed in the current setup (the corresponding switches are off). They are left untouched.

No changes in physics output are expected.

#### PR validation:

- [x] The full `HLT_75e33` menu still loads with the Phase-2 era (422 producers, 292 filters, 41 paths, 1 endpath).
- [x] Each finding was checked against the consuming C++ code (`PFECALSuperClusterAlgo.cc`, `HLTrigReport.cc`, `TracksterLinksProducer.cc`).
- [x] `runTheMatrix.py -l ph2_hlt`

#### PR description:

This PR modifies the BTL 2025 test beam setup previously proposed for the DUTbehind scenario (the most studied so far), and removes, for the time being, the DUTinFront scenario. The layout modifies the main mother volume structure, reshaping the top level volumes so as to maintain the minimal hierarchy required by the BTL numbering scheme encoded in ```BTLDetId```. REF and DUT modules are simply put along the z axis, and the beam gun fires along this direction. 

There are overlaps among ReadOut volumes that are irrelevant, as they are mostly empty logical volumes, except for the modules, that are verified to be correctly positioned according the specifications in https://indico.cern.ch/event/1695132/contributions/7128265/attachments/3289238/5880833/News__TB_Sep25__05_06_2026.pdf slide 45 - 47.

#### PR validation:

All configuration runs and provide meaningful validation output, taking into account the completely different setup wrt regular BTL. For a serious analysis a dedicated code needs to be written. Please note that the new ALPAKA-based rechits are not run at present, as the code possibly requiring them, in validation, is for the time being separately run.

#### PR description:

This PR updates the Phase-2 HLT timing/memory benchmarking tools in `HLTrigger/Configuration`:

1. **`runHLTTiming.sh`**: move the benchmark to geometry **D128**
   - input dataset switched to the `CMSSW_20_1_0_pre4` D128 TTbar PU RelVal:
     `/RelValTTbar_14TeV/CMSSW_20_1_0_pre4-PU_200X_mcRun4_realistic_v1_STD_D128_RegeneratedGS_PU_20261012_192421_RV32-v1/GEN-SIM-DIGI-RAW`
   - `--geometry ExtendedRun4D121`  `ExtendedRun4D128`
   - `--era Phase2C22I13M9`  `Phase2C26I13M9`

2. **`compareMemoryProfiles.py`**: layout fixes for the memory comparison plots
   - the supplementary label (`--cms-label`) is now passed directly to `hep.cms.label`, so mplhep places it next to the "CMS" logo instead of using hard-coded axes coordinates, which made the two overlap
   - the legend has been moved from outside the axes to inside the canvas, just below the statistics box
   - the y-axis range is now computed from where the stats box and legend actually end, rather than using a fixed `1.30  peak`, so the curves and peak annotations never overlap them, whatever the number of inputs or the label length

These are technical changes to the testing scripts only. No changes to any HLT menu or physics output are expected.

#### PR validation:

- `compareMemoryProfiles.py` tested in both single-file and two-file modes (`--gpu` and CPU), with the plots checked by eye: no label overlap, legend and stats box clear of the curves (example plot attached)
